No legacy-era API appears anywhere.

app/src/routes/(home).ts:19,27 + app/src/client/interactions.ts:13,24-30 — URL/URLSearchParams for filter state on both server and client

platform.rationale: Platform-first for data transport, URL handling, arrays/sets, and progressive enhancement; loses a point for unbounded upstream fetches (no AbortSignal.timeout) and duplicated regex URL parsing where URL would be cleaner.

evidence: app/package.json:10-18 — exactly four runtime deps (framework, hono, @hono/node-server, lit) plus vite as devDep; no CSS framework, no lodash/axios, no client router
app/server.mjs:1-9 — hono + @hono/node-server are the minimal pieces needed to serve Gracile's documented hono adapter
app/package.json:14 — lit 3.3 kept explicit, which the docs require for the lit dedupe/multiple-versions warning even though app code never imports it directly
dependencies.rationale: Minimal, modern, well-maintained, and all at current majors; every package earns its place, and the framework's peer (lit) is correctly pinned rather than installed blindly.

evidence: app/src/lib/api.ts + app/src/lib/data.ts — all API access and shaping behind two modules; no route fetches directly, and routes/ never touches framework internals (only documented exports)
app/src/lib/format.ts:1-31 — all display formatting centralized
app/src/lib/api.ts:22 — references `res`, which is undefined in this module (only an ambient global); the latent ReferenceError shipped to production in app/dist/server/chunk/data.js:32

app/ — no tsconfig.json and no typescript/@types/node devDeps, though the docs' minimal boilerplate ships `check: tsc` and `@gracile/gracile/tsconfigs/strictest`; nothing type-checks, which is precisely what let the `res` bug through
app/src/lib/data.ts:26 and app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:60 — `api<any>` and untyped context.props.GET.data propagate `any` through the whole boundary (11 type lines in 848 significant LOC)

app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].ts:46-60, moves/[name].ts:20-36, types/[name].ts:18-33, abilities/[name].ts:16-31, 404.ts — identical not-found markup and title ternary copy-pasted five ways while a shared notFound() helper sits unused at app/src/lib/components.ts:43
app/src/lib/api.ts:25 — promise-level cache stores rejections forever; one transient upstream failure permanently serves null until process restart
app/src/lib/api.ts:4 — dead ApiError class never thrown; app/src/lib/components.ts:50 dead sectionHeading export
churn_resistance.rationale: The data-access boundary and single-point configuration are genuinely well-factored and no framework internals are touched, so a Gracile upgrade would be cheap — but the absent TypeScript setup (the framework's own type-safety story), pervasive `any`, and five-way duplication of the 404 path mean requirement changes ripple widely and bugs ship silently.

findings.issue: The non-ok branch throws `new Error(`HTTP ${res.status} ${res.statusText}`)` but `res` is not defined in this module; it throws a ReferenceError instead of a diagnostic (and the bug is live in app/dist/server/chunk/data.js:32). The unused ApiError class at api.ts:4 shows the original intent.
findings.suggestion: Use `response.status`/`response.statusText`, or better `throw new ApiError(response.status, url)` and delete the dead class.

findings.issue: No tsconfig.json, no `typescript`/`@types/node` devDependencies, no typecheck script — nothing validates the TS sources, and Gracile's `defineRoute` typed-props feature is never actually exercised. This is what allowed the `res` bug to reach production.
findings.suggestion: Add `{ "extends": "@gracile/gracile/tsconfigs/strictest" }` plus a `check: tsc` script, per the framework's Installation docs.

findings.issue: The promise-level cache stores rejections forever with no TTL or invalidation, so a single upstream hiccup permanently poisons that resource (route shows 'Not found') until the process restarts.
findings.suggestion: Only memoize on success (e.g. `p.then(v => { cache.set(url, v); return v; }).catch(e => { cache.delete(url); throw e; })`), and consider a TTL.

findings.issue: The not-found markup and the 'Not found – Pokédex' title ternary are copy-pasted across four route files plus 404.ts, while the shared notFound() helper in components.ts:43 is never imported — a 404 design change edits five files.
findings.suggestion: Extract a notFoundRoute() helper (document + template) in lib/components.ts and reuse it in all five places.

findings.issue: Server-side fetch has no timeout/abort signal, so a hung upstream request hangs the page request and ties up a mapLimit worker indefinitely.
ID-from-URL extraction is a hand-rolled regex, and a second, subtly different copy exists at routes/(home).ts:60.
findings.suggestion: Keep one helper (or parse with `new URL(u).pathname.split('/')`) and use it everywhere.

findings.issue: `api<T = any>` default plus `any` in every destructure leaves the whole PokeAPI boundary untyped, so upstream data-shape changes surface as runtime render bugs rather than compile errors.
findings.suggestion: Declare minimal interfaces for the endpoints actually consumed (Species, Pokemon, Move, Ability, Type, Generation) and type `api<Species>(...)`.

findings.issue: Dead code: ApiError is exported but never thrown; sectionHeading in components.ts:50 is also unused.
findings.suggestion: Use ApiError in the error branch (see finding 1) and delete unused exports.

findings.issue: Inconsistent error handling: this route wraps `api()` in `.catch(() => null)` while every other route uses the shared tryApi helper.
findings.suggestion: Make getAbilityPage use tryApi for a single, uniform failure path.

summary: This app is squarely on Gracile's current stable release and its current idioms — 0.11.0's defineRoute/handler/props pipeline, the documented URL+import.meta.url asset notation for server output, the hono adapter, and a lean four-package runtime — so a framework upgrade would touch very little. The platform is used natively and well (fetch, URL/URLSearchParams, modern arrays, progressive-enhancement forms). The weak spot is longevity: there is no TypeScript setup at all (the framework's tsconfig presets and `tsc` check are skipped), the API boundary is `any`-typed, the 404 path is duplicated five ways, and a real `res`-is-undefined bug shipped to the production bundle because nothing type-checks.
